name: Caleb
description: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest

points: Caleb stilled the people and said, Let us go up at once and possess it, for we are well able to overcome it. Caleb showed faith and courage: the Most High already said he would deliver the enemy into our hands, so their stature did not matter.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes.

For they are bread for us. They said, they are food for us, we can take them by the power of the Lord. It said Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes, meaning they were furious and sorrowful for the false report that was given. So Joshua and Caleb did have a different kind of spirit on them, because they did not go with the general populace with their false report. How do you know not to go along with what a populace is saying when it is contrary to the Lord? The spirit of God must be upon you.

But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it. Hold on. This is very important. As the Lord goes into how the nation, all those over the age of twenty, are not going to make it into the land, he said something very telling about Caleb. So was Caleb moving in the same spirit as everyone else? No. He had a different kind of spirit on him.

But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land. Out of all the people that came out of Egypt, only Caleb and Joshua saw that land; the men that came out died in the wilderness and their children went in. That is how rebellious we were, and that is how rebellious we still are.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: But His servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully, would be brought into the land, and his seed should possess it.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

points: The tenth provocation was the report of the spies, and it was the last: how long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, because Caleb had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.

Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High.

Christ said the same thing: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. If the Lord finds you lukewarm, choosing your kids, your parents, or your spouse over following God and Christ and keeping the commandments wholly, you will not enter into the land; you must follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

points: The Lord heard their words and was wroth and sware: not one of the men of that evil generation would see the good land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, because he wholly followed the Lord, and Joshua the son of Nun, who would cause Israel to inherit it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

points: Joshua blessed him and gave Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance, and it became his inheritance unto this day, because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

points: Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.

note.label: Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah

points: He went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir, whose name before was Kirjathsepher, and said, he that smiteth Kirjathsepher and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife. Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it, and got Achsah to wife.

note.label: Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah

points: Caleb offers Achsah his daughter to wife to whoever smites Kirjath-sepher, and Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, takes it. Achsah asks her father for a blessing, springs of water with the south land, and Caleb gives her the upper springs and the nether springs.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: Hebron is given unto Caleb, as Moses said, and he expels thence the three sons of Anak.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: There was a very great man in Maon whose possessions were in Carmel, three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, shearing his sheep in Carmel. His name was Nabal, and his wife was Abigail, a woman of good understanding and of a beautiful countenance; but the man was churlish and evil in his doings, and he was of the house of Caleb.

note.label: 1 Samuel 25: Nabal's Folly and Abigail's Wisdom
